intervention_as_stated: Proiect Twinning „Consolidarea capacităților Inspectoratului General pentru Migrație pentru punerea în aplicare a legislației privind gestionarea migrației și azilul în conformitate cu acquis-ul Uniunii Europene”

summary: Return decisions are rising for visa-free CIS citizens who broke residence rules, including by working without a residence permit.
extraction_note: Return is out of scope except where directly about the right to work; extracted for the reference to working without a residence permit. The next sentence (causes of return decisions, including work in breach of the law) is not extracted separately.

text_en: Regarding the grounds for applying this measure to foreigners, entry bans for non-compliance with the rules of stay in the Republic of Moldova predominate, followed by bans for illegal work activity; the other categories are not significant.
summary: Entry bans were mostly for breaking residence rules, followed by bans for illegal work.
extraction_note: 221 entry bans were applied in 2025 (page 37); the text gives no count by ground.

text_en: The draft law was registered and assigned the unique number 507/MAI; it has also gone through the opinion procedure with the European Commission.
summary: The draft law on admission, stay and supervision of foreigners was registered as 507/MAI and went through European Commission review.
extraction_note: The law's title is in the list heading before the quote. The passage does not mention work; tagged chapter as the draft law on the regime of foreigners, which the run record lists among the Chapter 2 sources (rules on work permits for foreigners). For the analyst to confirm in pass 2.
intervention_as_stated: Proiectul de lege privind admisia, șederea și supravegherea străinilor în Republica Moldova

text_en: The provisions of Directive (EU) 2016/801 of the European Parliament and of the Council of 11 May 2016 on the conditions of entry and residence of third-country nationals for the purposes of research, studies, training, voluntary service, pupil exchange schemes or educational projects and au pairing will be regulated in the draft law on the admission, stay and supervision of foreigners in the Republic of Moldova.
summary: Directive 2016/801 on third-country researchers, students, trainees, volunteers and au pairs will be transposed through the draft law on foreigners.
extraction_note: Doubtful whether this belongs to Chapter 2 as bounded in the run record: the directive covers researchers, trainees and au pairs (work-related) but also students and volunteers. For the analyst.

The law establishes the regulatory framework for the exercise of the right to free movement, residence and equal treatment by citizens of the European Union, citizens of states signatory to the Schengen Agreement and their family members on the territory of the Republic of Moldova, and the application of restrictive measures on grounds of national security, public order and public health.
summary: Law 200/2025 sets the framework for EU and Schengen-state citizens and their families to move, reside and be treated equally in Moldova.
extraction_note: Listed among IGM's contributions to the regulatory framework; recorded as adopted because the law has a number. The text does not give the date of adoption or entry into force. "Republici i" is kept as converted.
intervention_as_stated: Legea nr.200/2025 privind libera circulație și șederea pe teritoriul Republicii Moldova a cetățenilor Uniunii Europene și a membrilor familiilor acestora

summary: In January 2025 IGM proposed amending the decision on the fingerprint register information system to meet EURODAC requirements.

intervention_as_stated: Hotărârea Guvernului nr. 565/2007 privind aprobarea Sistemului informațional automatizat „Registrul dactiloscopic”

intervention_as_stated: Sistemul informațional „Migrație”

text_en: Over 130,000 Ukrainian refugees in Moldova, primarily skilled women, represent an untapped economic asset.
summary: The brief says over 130,000 Ukrainian refugees in Moldova, mostly skilled women, are an untapped economic asset.

text_en: Despite documented labour shortages, only 29 percent of working-age refugees are in paid work.
summary: Only 29 percent of working-age refugees are in paid work despite labour shortages.
extraction_note: The reference period is the SERHC 2024 survey on which the brief draws (page 4); the brief also gives 34 percent for paid work since arrival at page 3 (item -0024), and 29 percent at page 3 (item -0026).

text_en: Survey findings point to systemic barriers: language gaps (36 percent of job seekers), skills mismatch and non-recognition of diplomas (13 percent), and scarce, affordable childcare.
summary: Survey findings point to language gaps, skills mismatch and non-recognition of diplomas, and scarce affordable childcare as barriers.
extraction_note: Summary statement; the barriers are detailed at page 2.

text_en: While Temporary Protection (TP) grants the right to work, these obstacles drive underemployment and reliance on social assistance.
summary: Temporary protection grants refugees the right to work, but the obstacles drive underemployment and reliance on social assistance.
extraction_note: States the legal position (temporary protection grants the right to work) and that the barriers cause underemployment; recorded as a finding, though the second half could be read as a barrier.

text_en: Recommended measures include sector-specific Romanian language programmes, fast-track credential recognition, expansion of subsidized childcare, micro-grants for entrepreneurship, and employer-focused job-matching through the Agenția Națională pentru Ocuparea Forței de Muncă (ANOFM)—Moldovan National Employment Agency.
summary: Recommended: sector-specific Romanian courses, fast-track credential recognition, more subsidised childcare, entrepreneurship micro-grants and employer-focused job matching through ANOFM.
extraction_note: Summary of the recommendations set out at page 4.

text_en: Refugees seeking employment often encounter Romanian-language requirements, unclear regulations, informal hiring practices, scarce childcare, and limited access to credit, training, and information.
summary: Refugees seeking jobs often face Romanian-language requirements, unclear regulations, informal hiring, scarce childcare and limited access to credit, training and information.

text_en: Testimonies reveal a large share of people who are unemployed, in precarious jobs, and experiencing rising psychological stress, even though labour shortages persist in agriculture, hospitality, social care, construction, and IT.
summary: Testimonies show many refugees unemployed or in precarious jobs, although labour shortages persist in several sectors.

text_en: Temporary protection status formally grants unrestricted access to work, yet in practice, many refugees accept low-skilled positions because vacancies in their own professions are rare, and employers often require different skill sets.
summary: Temporary protection formally gives unrestricted access to work, but many refugees take low-skilled jobs as vacancies in their professions are rare.
extraction_note: States the legal position and a cause of underemployment in one sentence; recorded as a finding, though the cause could be read as a barrier.

text_en: Fragmented, underfunded support services further blunt integration efforts.
summary: Fragmented and underfunded support services weaken integration efforts.
extraction_note: "Integration" here follows the paragraph on refugees' access to work and employment.

text_en: The potential is substantial as more than 80 percent of working-age refugee respondents (18–64 years) report having professional experience, 77 percent hold vocational or higher qualifications, and 63 percent are keen to join self-employment programmes.
summary: Over 80 percent of working-age refugee respondents report professional experience, 77 percent vocational or higher qualifications, and 63 percent want self-employment programmes.
extraction_note: Page 3 gives 81 percent with experience and 76 percent with at least vocational or tertiary education (item -0024).

text_en: Only 29 percent, however, have found paid work, over half of households rely mainly on social assistance, and nearly half of job seekers cite insufficient Romanian language as their primary barrier to employment.
summary: Only 29 percent found paid work; over half of households rely on social assistance; nearly half of jobseekers cite Romanian as the main barrier.
extraction_note: "Nearly half" of job seekers citing language differs from the 36 percent given at page 1 and page 2 (items -0003 and -0013); recorded as printed.

text_en: Targeted language courses, affordable childcare, streamlined recognition of qualifications, and coordinated funding could unlock the potential of this workforce and benefit Moldova’s economy.
summary: Targeted language courses, affordable childcare, streamlined recognition of qualifications and coordinated funding could unlock this workforce's potential.
extraction_note: Phrased as what could unlock the potential ("could"), read as a recommendation.

text_en: Limited Romanian language skills are the most frequently cited obstacle for adult refugees. Approximately 36 percent of refugees report this as a significant barrier to employment.
summary: Limited Romanian is the obstacle adult refugees cite most; about 36 percent call it a significant barrier to employment.
extraction_note: Two sentences on one claim; the figure could also be a metric.

text_en: Around 13 percent of refugees cannot find job openings relevant to their professional background or education level. This leads to underemployment or engaging in time-bound/seasonal employment, as many highly skilled individuals are offered low-skilled jobs or jobs outside their expertise.
summary: About 13 percent of refugees find no jobs matching their background, leading to underemployment or seasonal work.
extraction_note: Two sentences on one claim.

text_en: Barriers to the recognition of foreign credentials also persist.
summary: Barriers to recognising foreign credentials persist.

text_en: A lack of affordable childcare is a major constraint, especially since most refugees are women and often sole caregivers. While this issue is common for both refugees and host community members, 11 percent of refugee households cited limited access to childcare as a barrier to employment.
summary: Lack of affordable childcare is a major constraint for refugee women; 11 percent of refugee households cite it as a barrier to employment.
extraction_note: Two sentences on one claim. Extracted because the brief states childcare as a barrier to employment; childcare policy itself is outside Chapter 2.

text_en: Around 10 percent of refugees perceive that salaries in Moldova are too low compared to what they earned in Ukraine. The income gap, combined with rising inflation and living costs, can discourage skilled refugees from accepting offers of employment.
summary: About 10 percent of refugees find Moldovan salaries too low, which can discourage skilled refugees from accepting jobs.
extraction_note: Two sentences on one claim. The following paragraph on household income and access to credit is not extracted (poverty and financial inclusion).

text_en: Around 2 percent of refugees lack information on how and where to look for jobs in Moldova. For 39 percent, support with identification and job matching is the most preferred form of assistance to secure employment.
summary: About 2 percent of refugees lack information on job searching; 39 percent most prefer support with job identification and matching.
extraction_note: Two sentences, one metric item.

text_en: Formal employment services, like ANOFM, remain underutilized.
summary: Formal employment services such as ANOFM remain underused by refugees.

text_en: While the legal framework is not the primary barrier, administrative challenges can still slow down labour market integration.
summary: The legal framework is not the main barrier, but administrative challenges can slow refugees' labour market integration.

text_en: Some employers are reluctant to hire refugees due to assumed legal complexities or limited awareness of candidates’ skills and qualifications.
summary: Some employers are reluctant to hire refugees because of assumed legal complexity or limited awareness of their skills.

text_en: Although language proficiency is the most frequently cited individual barrier, a broader analysis suggests that structural weaknesses in Moldova’s labour market—such as skills mismatches, low wages, and limited job availability—represent the main constraints to employment. Taken together, these systemic factors outweigh specific integration challenges such as language or childcare needs.
summary: The brief's analysis suggests structural labour market weaknesses, not language or childcare, are the main constraints on refugees' employment.
extraction_note: Two sentences on one claim. The sentence that follows (need for longer-term reforms) is extracted separately as item -0023.

text_en: This indicates that many of the key impediments are structural and affect both refugees and the host population, pointing to the need for longer-term labour market and economic reforms rather than short-term programmatic interventions.
summary: The brief says the impediments are structural and call for longer-term labour market and economic reforms rather than short-term programmes.
extraction_note: Could be read as a lesson (what matters and why) or as a recommendation (the need for longer-term reforms); recorded as a recommendation. It concerns the labour market generally, affecting refugees and the host population.

text_en: 76 percent of adult refugees have at least vocational or tertiary education, and 81 percent report having previous professional work experience. However, only 34 percent have engaged in paid work since arriving in Moldova.
summary: 76 percent of adult refugees have vocational or tertiary education and 81 percent work experience, but only 34 percent have had paid work in Moldova.
extraction_note: The 34 percent differs from the 29 percent given for paid work since arrival a few lines below (item -0026) and at pages 1 and 2; recorded as printed. Quote starts after the label "Strong Skills and Experience:".

text_en: Refugees demonstrate strong motivation to become self-reliant, with 22 percent actively looking for work in the four weeks before the survey. Notably, 63 percent expressed interest in a self-employment support programme.
summary: 22 percent of refugees were actively seeking work in the four weeks before the survey; 63 percent want a self-employment programme.
extraction_note: Quote starts after the label "Willingness to Work and Adapt:".

text_en: Despite the challenges, around 29 percent of refugees have engaged in paid work since arriving in Moldova.
summary: About 29 percent of refugees have had paid work since arriving in Moldova.
extraction_note: Conflicts with 34 percent for the same indicator in item -0024; recorded as printed.

text_en: Most employed refugees (around 61 percent) found jobs through friends or acquaintances, highlighting the role of informal networks and community connections in facilitating employment.
summary: About 61 percent of employed refugees found jobs through friends or acquaintances.

text_en: Expand employment-focused Romanian language courses.
summary: Expand employment-focused Romanian language courses for refugees.

text_en: Implement fast-track diploma recognition programmes and organize refugee employment fairs, complemented by increased outreach and strengthened assistance through ANOFM.
summary: Introduce fast-track diploma recognition and refugee job fairs, with more outreach and assistance through ANOFM.

text_en: Simplify procedures for registering self-employment and/or establishing an individual legal entity and provide micro-grants alongside mentorship to support refugee entrepreneurship.
summary: Simplify registration of self-employment or an individual legal entity and give refugees micro-grants with mentoring.
extraction_note: Extracted as access of foreign nationals to self-employment; the other Care and Finance recommendations (childcare services, microfinance) are not extracted.

text_en: Continue providing legal work permits and actively promote employment opportunities to both refugees and local businesses.
summary: Continue providing legal work permits and promote employment opportunities to refugees and local businesses.

text_en: Implemented through clear lead agencies and partner coordination, these measures can accelerate inclusion and reduce fiscal pressure.
summary: The recommended measures should be implemented through clear lead agencies and partner coordination, which can speed inclusion and reduce fiscal pressure.
extraction_note: Second-pass addition (PC-05). Refers to the measures listed in the preceding sentence (item -0005). Read as a recommendation on how to implement them; it could also be read as a finding on their likely effect ("can"), hence ambiguous_type and hedged.

text_en: The Ukrainian refugee population in Moldova presents a significant talent pool that could be leveraged better in the labour market
summary: Ukrainian refugees in Moldova are a significant talent pool that could be better used in the labour market.
extraction_note: Second-pass addition (PC-05). Lead statement of the section, a claim of its own (rules section 5); the converted text has no full stop. Similar in substance to the opening claim on page 1 (item -0001) but worded differently; short document, so extracted at each place (pass 2 may link with same_as_earlier).
